      const h = req.headers;
      const country = (h['cf-ipcountry'] ?? h['x-vercel-ip-country'] ?? h['x-country']) as string | undefined;
      const input: PageHitInput = {
        ts: Date.now(),
        path,
        status: reply.statusCode,
        ip: req.ip,
        ua: String(h['user-agent'] ?? ''),
        referer: h.referer as string | undefined,
        host: h.host as string | undefined,
        country,

      const token = isBot(input.ua) ? null : sessionCookie(h.cookie);
      // Identity lookup runs detached: the response is already sent, and any
      // failure just records the hit anonymously.
      void (async () => {
        try {
          if (token) input.userEmail = await verifyClerkToken('Bearer ' + token);

      })();
    } catch { /* recording must never break a response */ }
  });

    timer = setInterval(() => { void flushPageHits(); }, FLUSH_MS);

// Tiny click beacon injected into every HTML document so clicks are captured
// host-wide (SPA shell + every static-path app) without touching sibling repos.
// Never reads input values other than type submit/button.
export const BEACON_JS = `(function(){try{
if(location.pathname.indexOf('/admin')===0)return;
var S='a,button,[role=button],summary,input[type=submit],input[type=button],[data-track]';
document.addEventListener('click',function(e){try{
var t=e.target;if(!t||!t.closest)return;
var el=t.closest(S);if(!el)return;
var tag=el.tagName.toLowerCase();
var label=el.getAttribute('aria-label');
if(!label){label=(el.textContent||'').replace(/\\s+/g,' ').trim();
if(!label&&tag==='input'&&(el.type==='submit'||el.type==='button'))label=el.value||''}
navigator.sendBeacon('/api/analytics/click',JSON.stringify({path:location.pathname,tag:tag,id:el.id||'',label:String(label).slice(0,80),href:el.getAttribute('href')||''}))
}catch(x){}},true)
}catch(x){}})();`;

async function toHtml(payload: unknown): Promise<string | null> {
  if (typeof payload === 'string') return payload;
  if (Buffer.isBuffer(payload)) return payload.toString('utf-8');
  if (payload && typeof (payload as any).pipe === 'function') {
    const chunks: Buffer[] = [];
    for await (const chunk of payload as AsyncIterable<Buffer | string>) {
      chunks.push(typeof chunk === 'string' ? Buffer.from(chunk) : chunk);
    }
    return Buffer.concat(chunks).toString('utf-8');
  }
  return null;
}

export function registerClickBeacon(app: FastifyInstance): void {
  app.addHook('onSend', async (req, reply, payload) => {
    if (isBlogVideoPath(req.url)) return payload;
    const ctype = String(reply.getHeader('content-type') ?? '');
    if (!ctype.startsWith('text/html')) return payload;
    if (/^\s*attachment\b/i.test(String(reply.getHeader('content-disposition') ?? ''))) return payload;
    const html = await toHtml(payload);
    if (html === null) return payload;
    const nonce = (req as any).cspNonce as string | undefined;
    const tag = `<script${nonce ? ` nonce="${nonce}"` : ''}>${BEACON_JS}</script>`;
    let idx = html.search(/<\/head>/i);
    if (idx === -1) idx = html.search(/<\/body>/i);
    reply.removeHeader('content-length');
    if (idx === -1) return html;
    return html.slice(0, idx) + tag + html.slice(idx);
  });
}

export function registerPageHitRecorder(app: FastifyInstance, opts: { flush?: boolean } = {}): void {
  app.addHook('onResponse', async (req, reply) => {
    try {
      if (req.method !== 'GET') return;
      const path = req.url.split('?')[0];
      if (path.startsWith('/api/')) return;
      const ct = String(reply.getHeader('content-type') ?? '');
      if (!ct.toLowerCase().startsWith('text/html')) return;

      const h = req.headers;
      const country = (h['cf-ipcountry'] ?? h['x-vercel-ip-country'] ?? h['x-country']) as string | undefined;
      const input: PageHitInput = {
        ts: Date.now(),
        path,
        status: reply.statusCode,
        ip: req.ip,
        ua: String(h['user-agent'] ?? ''),
        referer: h.referer as string | undefined,
        host: h.host as string | undefined,
        country,
      };
      const token = isBot(input.ua) ? null : sessionCookie(h.cookie);
      // Identity lookup runs detached: the response is already sent, and any
      // failure just records the hit anonymously.
      void (async () => {
        try {
          if (token) input.userEmail = await verifyClerkToken('Bearer ' + token);
        } catch { /* anonymous */ }
        try { recordPageHit(input); } catch { /* never break the server */ }
      })();
    } catch { /* recording must never break a response */ }
  });

  if (opts.flush !== false && !timer) {
    timer = setInterval(() => { void flushPageHits(); }, FLUSH_MS);
    timer.unref?.();
    app.addHook('onClose', async () => {
import type { FastifyInstance } from 'fastify';
import { isBlogVideoPath } from './security-headers.js';

// Tiny click beacon injected into every HTML document so clicks are captured
// host-wide (SPA shell + every static-path app) without touching sibling repos.
// Never reads input values other than type submit/button.
export const BEACON_JS = `(function(){try{
if(location.pathname.indexOf('/admin')===0)return;
var S='a,button,[role=button],summary,input[type=submit],input[type=button],[data-track]';
document.addEventListener('click',function(e){try{
var t=e.target;if(!t||!t.closest)return;
var el=t.closest(S);if(!el)return;
var tag=el.tagName.toLowerCase();
var label=el.getAttribute('aria-label');
if(!label){label=(el.textContent||'').replace(/\\s+/g,' ').trim();
if(!label&&tag==='input'&&(el.type==='submit'||el.type==='button'))label=el.value||''}
navigator.sendBeacon('/api/analytics/click',JSON.stringify({path:location.pathname,tag:tag,id:el.id||'',label:String(label).slice(0,80),href:el.getAttribute('href')||''}))
}catch(x){}},true)
}catch(x){}})();`;

async function toHtml(payload: unknown): Promise<string | null> {
  if (typeof payload === 'string') return payload;
  if (Buffer.isBuffer(payload)) return payload.toString('utf-8');
  if (payload && typeof (payload as any).pipe === 'function') {
    const chunks: Buffer[] = [];
    for await (const chunk of payload as AsyncIterable<Buffer | string>) {
      chunks.push(typeof chunk === 'string' ? Buffer.from(chunk) : chunk);
    }
    return Buffer.concat(chunks).toString('utf-8');
  }
  return null;
}

export function registerClickBeacon(app: FastifyInstance): void {
  app.addHook('onSend', async (req, reply, payload) => {
    if (isBlogVideoPath(req.url)) return payload;
    const ctype = String(reply.getHeader('content-type') ?? '');
    if (!ctype.startsWith('text/html')) return payload;
    if (/^\s*attachment\b/i.test(String(reply.getHeader('content-disposition') ?? ''))) return payload;
    const html = await toHtml(payload);
    if (html === null) return payload;
    const nonce = (req as any).cspNonce as string | undefined;
    const tag = `<script${nonce ? ` nonce="${nonce}"` : ''}>${BEACON_JS}</script>`;
    let idx = html.search(/<\/head>/i);
    if (idx === -1) idx = html.search(/<\/body>/i);
    reply.removeHeader('content-length');
    if (idx === -1) return html;
    return html.slice(0, idx) + tag + html.slice(idx);
  });
}

## §13 Queueing PRDs from external automation

Decision: is the session-manager app running on this machine right now?
- Yes → call the `scheduler_create_prd` MCP tool, with the usual fields (`title`, `cwd`, `estimateMinutes`, `sourcePromptId`, `goal`, `acceptanceCriteria`, `implementationNotes`) plus `gate` and `files` (§6).
- No → stop. Ask the human to start the app, then call the tool again. Never write the PRD file by hand: the scheduler quarantines a file the API did not write, and it never runs.

It only works while the app is running — closing it removes the admin port/token, and the call fails with `session-manager app is not running (admin API unreachable)`.

---

## §14 A parked job may resolve itself now

Rule: if a job parks `needs_review` with verdict `transcript_errors`, `no_verdict_sentinel`, or `abandoned_background_task`, do nothing first. The scheduler re-runs the gate on its own and completes the job once the gate is green, the commit is on HEAD, and the tracked tree is clean.
Why: those three verdicts mean the transcript looked noisy, not that the work was wrong.

Rule: a park caused by a DIFFERENT actor already finishing the same objective (a sibling PRD, a human) does not self-heal this way. Why: the job has no landed commit of its own. Confirm in the tree that the work is really done, then call `scheduler_archive_prd` with the slug. Archiving marks the job completed and frees the PRDs that depend on it. Never hand-edit `queue.json`: the scheduler and the watchdog both write it. Archiving clears a stale label; it does not fix a real bug.

Known gap: `pass_no_commit` ("already correct, nothing to commit") isn't yet in the self-heal list above for the general case.

---

## §15 Pre-queue checklist (the litany)

Before queueing a new PRD, verify each of these:

- [ ] **§1 Bounded waits:** every poll loop has a `for i in $(seq 1 N)` cap ≤20 iterations; no uptime/restart signal used to detect a static-content deploy.
- [ ] **Every command bounded:** every test/build/deploy command is wrapped in `timeout` (typecheck/unit 300s, e2e 120s, `curl --max-time 15`).
- [ ] **§2 No bonus work:** the AC list is the only source of work.
- [ ] **§3 Verify, don't poll:** every deploy/migration step is followed by a test command that exits 1 on failure; the AC test command ran green once before you declare done.
- [ ] **§4 Bounded generators:** any search/seed loop has an explicit max and surfaces failure on exhaustion.
- [ ] **§5 Frontmatter:** `title`, `cwd` (exists on this machine), `estimateMinutes` present; `dependsOn` used for ordering, not `parallelGroup`.
- [ ] **§6 Gate and files:** `gate` follows every rule in §6 (or is `["none"]` alone); `files` is 1–50 repo-relative paths, no overlap with a concurrent PRD.
- [ ] **§7 Self-contained:** no reference to "the conversation" or outside context; paths/identifiers inline; clean UTF-8, no NUL bytes (`grep -qP '\x00' file && echo BAD`).
- [ ] **§7 Worktree reach:** no relative path to a gitignored file; live-run steps use absolute main-checkout paths in an artifact-only PRD. Why: the job worktree has no gitignored runtime state, so relative paths fail or bake a temporary path into host config (burrow 1516).
- [ ] **§8 Scope:** targets ≤10 min, ceiling 15; e2e/publish sharded to one spec per PRD.
- [ ] **§9 Failure surfacing:** errors exit 1 with a diagnostic line; no silent `|| true`.
- [ ] **§10 Negative assertions:** every "should find nothing" check is inverted to exit 0 on the clean case.
- [ ] **§11 End green:** the gate runs last; any intentional failure runs early and is captured.
- [ ] **§12 No stranded probes:** a probe error is corrected or annotated; an expected `timeout` cap branches on exit 124.
- [ ] **Gate baseline:** every gate command ran green once at HEAD in the main checkout; a red suite is scoped to the PRD's own test files and the PRD notes say why. Why: a gate already red on base parks as `sentinel_fail`.
- [ ] **No human-only gates:** no gate or criterion needs a human or the passage of time (cron install, live post wait, live payment, dashboard action); those end `SCHEDULER_VERDICT: NEEDS_HUMAN <question>`. Why: no executor can pass them.

  These are the gaps I found after checking the draft against the code:
  
  1. **Pageview from `sendBeacon` loses its body.** `/api/analytics/pageview` never parses a string body; only the click route does `JSON.parse` on text/plain. Pageviews sent by the beacon would all record as `path '/'` with no ids. Fix: PRD 3 adds the same string-body parse to the pageview route.
  2. **Server-side telemetry ingest has no cookie fallback.** No PRD touches `server/routes/telemetry.ts`. Until all 14 host-kit consumers rebuild and republish, they keep sending sessionStorage ids, so their events and errors never join a session. Fix: PRD 3 (or a new PRD) makes `/api/telemetry/{event,log,error}` prefer cookie ids, keep the client ids as `client_*`, and record a republish rollout list.
  3. **Double pageviews on Session Manager pages.** `usePageView()` is also called in `src/pages/session-manager-landing/AccountChip.tsx:29` and `ManualPage.tsx:146`. Fix: PRD 4 removes all three calls, or makes the hook stop posting pageviews.
  4. **Nothing refreshes the 30-minute session after page load.** The server only sets cookies on HTML responses. A user clicking around inside the SPA for over 30 minutes lets the cookie expire, and each client then mints its own new id. Fix: one shared `touchSession()` rule (re-write `bilko_sid` Max-Age on every send, mint if missing). Define it in PRD 1 and have the beacon, `src/hooks/usePageView.ts` and host-kit follow it word for word.
  5. **The three PRDs that read ids can drift apart.** PRDs 4 and 5 run in parallel, and PRD 3 is independent of both. The body fields are named inconsistently (beacon `visitor_id`, column `client_vid`, new `track`, column `track_name`). Fix: PRD 1 exports the field names and cookie format; PRDs 3, 4 and 5 cite them.
  6. **Cookie values aren't validated.** `readSessionIds` would echo any attacker-set value back in Set-Cookie and store it. Fix: accept only UUID format, otherwise mint a new one; same check on body ids in PRD 3.
  7. **Duplicate timeline.** `/api/admin/traffic/visitor/:id` in `admin-observability.ts:356` already merges page_hits and click_events. PRD 6 builds a second timeline. Fix: share one query helper and add a session-id mode, rather than a parallel implementation.
  8. **Timestamp units differ across tables.** `page_hits`/`click_events` use `ts_ms`. `funnel_events.created_at` is DATETIME text. `app_errors`/`app_logs` `created_at` are INTEGER. `sessions.started_at` is INTEGER. Fix: PRD 6 normalizes everything to ms and tests a mixed-source ordering.
  9. **Wrong file for the new columns.** `ADDITIVE_COLUMNS` lives in `server/db-schema.ts`, not `server/db.ts`. Fix: PRD 2 edits db-schema.ts for columns and puts the indexes in the post-ALTER index batch in `db.ts:180` (indexes in MIGRATIONS run before the ALTERs and would fail on an existing DB).
  10. **Two planned indexes already exist.** `idx_page_views_session` and `idx_funnel_events_session` are already there. Fix: drop them from PRD 2. It still needs `page_hits(session_id)`, `click_events(session_id)`, `app_errors(session_id)` and `funnel_events(visitor_id)`.
  11. **Retention mismatch.** page_hits is pruned at 90 days. click_events, sessions and funnel_events have no matching prune, so old session timelines would be partial. Fix: PRD 6 caps the session list at 90 days, or PRD 2 adds a matching prune.
  12. **PII and privacy.** Joining sessions makes click labels (raw `textContent`, e.g. "Signed in as x@y.com") and `href` query strings (checkout or magic-link tokens) traceable to one person. Fix: PRD 4 scrubs emails and digits from labels, strips the query from `href`, and honors `data-track-redact`. PRD 10 updates the privacy page for the new 1-year first-party cookie.
  13. **Any app on the domain can read the ids.** The cookies are non-HttpOnly and every static-path app shares the origin. The `sessions.converted` flip trusts `session_id`+`visitor_id`. Fix: on the server, derive ids for conversion/purchase flags from the cookie only, never the body.
  14. **`replaceState` can flood pageviews.** Games and tools call `replaceState` on every query change, and pageview is rate-limited per visitor at 2x. Fix: PRD 4 dedupes on pathname only and ignores `replaceState` when the path is unchanged.
  15. **Legacy-id handover gap.** The first page_hit before the "localStorage wins" rewrite carries the server-minted vid. Fix: PRD 6 links the two ids through `client_vid` on the first pageview, or PRD 4 back-fills that session's rows.
  16. **host-kit default endpoint.** Switching to a relative `/api/telemetry` breaks consumers that run cross-origin (local dev, `external-url` apps). Fix: PRD 5 uses relative only when `location.hostname` is bilko.run or localhost on the host port, otherwise the absolute host.
  17. **Validation and process gaps.** PRD 11 needs a check that no `/api/*` or non-200 response sets cookies and that `cache-control: private, no-store` stays on every HTML response that does. PRD 5 also needs the `pnpm --filter host-kit build` step and the changeset.

11 validate.","agentId":"a03d9c5379f5b6338","agentType":"general-purpose","harnessNoteCount":0,"harnessTailCount":0,"harnessSectionHash":"b35b08f6c9988e79","content":[{"type":"text","text":"These are the gaps I found after checking the draft against the code:

1. **Pageview from `sendBeacon` loses its body.** `/api/analytics/pageview` never parses a string body; only the click route does `JSON.parse` on text/plain. Pageviews sent by the beacon would all record as `path '/'` with no ids. Fix: PRD 3 adds the same string-body parse to the pageview route.
2. **Server-side telemetry ingest has no cookie fallback.** No PRD touches `server/routes/telemetry.ts`. Until all 14 host-kit consumers rebuild and republish, they keep sending sessionStorage ids, so their events and errors never join a session. Fix: PRD 3 (or a new PRD) makes `/api/telemetry/{event,log,error}` prefer cookie ids, keep the client ids as `client_*`, and record a republish rollout list.
3. **Double pageviews on Session Manager pages.** `usePageView()` is also called in `src/pages/session-manager-landing/AccountChip.tsx:29` and `ManualPage.tsx:146`. Fix: PRD 4 removes all three calls, or makes the hook stop posting pageviews.
4. **Nothing refreshes the 30-minute session after page load.** The server only sets cookies on HTML responses. A user clicking around inside the SPA for over 30 minutes lets the cookie expire, and each client then mints its own new id. Fix: one shared `touchSession()` rule (re-write `bilko_sid` Max-Age on every send, mint if missing). Define it in PRD 1 and have the beacon, `src/hooks/usePageView.ts` and host-kit follow it word for word.
5. **The three PRDs that read ids can drift apart.** PRDs 4 and 5 run in parallel, and PRD 3 is independent of both. The body fields are named inconsistently (beacon `visitor_id`, column `client_vid`, new `track`, column `track_name`). Fix: PRD 1 exports the field names and cookie format; PRDs 3, 4 and 5 cite them.
6. **Cookie values aren't validated.** `readSessionIds` would echo any attacker-set value back in Set-Cookie and store it. Fix: accept only UUID format, otherwise mint a new one; same check on body ids in PRD 3.
7. **Duplicate timeline.** `/api/admin/traffic/visitor/:id` in `admin-observability.ts:356` already merges page_hits and click_events. PRD 6 builds a second timeline. Fix: share one query helper and add a session-id mode, rather than a parallel implementation.
8. **Timestamp units differ across tables.** `page_hits`/`click_events` use `ts_ms`. `funnel_events.created_at` is DATETIME text. `app_errors`/`app_logs` `created_at` are INTEGER. `sessions.started_at` is INTEGER. Fix: PRD 6 normalizes everything to ms and tests a mixed-source ordering.
9. **Wrong file for the new columns.** `ADDITIVE_COLUMNS` lives in `server/db-schema.ts`, not `server/db.ts`. Fix: PRD 2 edits db-schema.ts for columns and puts the indexes in the post-ALTER index batch in `db.ts:180` (indexes in MIGRATIONS run before the ALTERs and would fail on an existing DB).
10. **Two planned indexes already exist.** `idx_page_views_session` and `idx_funnel_events_session` are already there. Fix: drop them from PRD 2. It still needs `page_hits(session_id)`, `click_events(session_id)`, `app_errors(session_id)` and `funnel_events(visitor_id)`.
11. **Retention mismatch.** page_hits is pruned at 90 days. click_events, sessions and funnel_events have no matching prune, so old session timelines would be partial. Fix: PRD 6 caps the session list at 90 days, or PRD 2 adds a matching prune.
12. **PII and privacy.** Joining sessions makes click labels (raw `textContent`, e.g. "Signed in as x@y.com") and `href` query strings (checkout or magic-link tokens) traceable to one person. Fix: PRD 4 scrubs emails and digits from labels, strips the query from `href`, and honors `data-track-redact`. PRD 10 updates the privacy page for the new 1-year first-party cookie.
13. **Any app on the domain can read the ids.** The cookies are non-HttpOnly and every static-path app shares the origin. The `sessions.converted` flip trusts `session_id`+`visitor_id`. Fix: on the server, derive ids for conversion/purchase flags from the cookie only, never the body.
14. **`replaceState` can flood pageviews.** Games and tools call `replaceState` on every query change, and pageview is rate-limited per visitor at 2x. Fix: PRD 4 dedupes on pathname only and ignores `replaceState` when the path is unchanged.
15. **Legacy-id handover gap.** The first page_hit before the "localStorage wins" rewrite carries the server-minted vid. Fix: PRD 6 links the two ids through `client_vid` on the first pageview, or PRD 4 back-fills that session's rows.
16. **host-kit default endpoint.** Switching to a relative `/api/telemetry` breaks consumers that run cross-origin (local dev, `external-url` apps). Fix: PRD 5 uses relative only when `location.hostname` is bilko.run or localhost on the host port, otherwise the absolute host.
17. **Validation and process gaps.** PRD 11 needs a check that no `/api/*` or non-200 response sets cookies and that `cache-control: private, no-store` stays on every HTML response that does. {"parentUuid":"0f67bb3b-03bd-4ce6-99a1-56d52dc0921e","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-opus-5-5","id":"msg_011CgABT1muKPfEfDgND4XYj","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"I've queued the whole plan: 13 PRDs plus one validate PRD (#1348–#1361) in this Epic. Nothing has been built yet. The scheduler runs them headless, and a validator checks each one at the end.

**The plan in plain terms.** Today bilko.run has four separate ways of identifying a visitor (a per-tab id in the host app, server-side IP+browser hashes, nothing at all on clicks, and the host-kit's own per-tab id). So there's no single "session" to look at. The fix:

1. **One identity for the whole site.** The server sets two first-party cookies on every page: `bilko_vid` (visitor, kept 1 year) and `bilko_sid` (session, ends after 30 minutes idle, shared across tabs). Every capture path reads those same cookies.
2. **Automatic capture, no code needed in apps.** The click script the server already injects into every page now sends the session ids with each click. It also records a page view on first load and on every in-app navigation, which covers all `/projects/<slug>/` apps right away. It strips emails and long numbers from click labels and query strings from links. The host app's React page-view hook is removed so pages aren't counted twice.
3. **SDK for tagging flows.** host-kit's telemetry uses the shared session and sends to the same-origin endpoint. Calling `track()` without setup now works instead of being rejected. New `trackFlow(flow, step)` lets an app tag its main flows. Events from the 14 apps still on old host-kit builds also get matched to the right session on the server side, so they join sessions before those apps republish.
4. **Dashboard at `/admin/observability`.** A Sessions panel lists recent sessions; click one to see where the user landed, every page, click, event and error in order. A Flows panel shows a health row per app and a funnel per tagged flow.
5. **Adoption process.** A new `docs/observability.md`: what's captured for free, how to tag buttons and flows, privacy rules, how to check your app in the dashboard, how to roll out. The host contract (which other repos' sessions read through the bilko-host MCP), the host-kit README and the beacon doc are corrected to match. The privacy page will disclose the two cookies.

**Order:** session cookies and SDK first → database columns, beacon, telemetry matching, privacy page → click/page-view storage, hook removal, sessions API → flows API, Sessions panel → Flows panel, docs → validate.

# send-feedback

**Role:** the ONE channel for project-to-project communication. You are a
*courier*, never a fixer — you deliver a report into another project's inbox
and stop. You never edit the other project's files, never queue a PRD there,
and never wait for a reply.

## Why this exists

`/process-feedback`, `/my-feedback` and the `session-manager-operations/feedback/`
folder were retired (2026-08-02), and the scheduler was locked down so a PRD can
only JOIN an Epic a human already approved. Both were right. Together they left
no way to hand a finding across a project boundary. This skill is that way back
— narrowed to exactly one shape: **a proposal deposited in another project's
queue, which a human there must approve before anything runs.**

## The one hard rule

**Different project, or don't use this.** If the finding belongs to the project
you are already working in, run `/develop` inside the Epic you are already in.
The tool refuses `toCwd === fromCwd` outright, so getting this wrong costs you a
round-trip, not a wrong write.

| Finding belongs to | Route |
| --- | --- |
| The project you're in | `/develop` in your current Epic |
| Another project on this machine | this skill |
| Nothing actionable | say so explicitly |

Per the global core rules, routing a finding is the **default action, not a
question**. Do not ask "should I send this to X?" — send it, then report what
you delivered.

## Steps

### 1. Confirm it's really theirs

Before couriering anything, satisfy yourself the finding is about the other
project's behavior, not about how *your* project calls it. A misrouted report
costs a human in another repo their attention. If you can't tell, say which
project you think owns it and why, and send it anyway with that uncertainty
stated in the body — an honest "I think this is yours because X, but I couldn't
verify from here" is useful; a confident wrong claim is not.

### 2. Resolve the target cwd — never guess it

```
feedback_list_projects()
```

Returns every project on this machine that can receive feedback (each already
has a `session-manager-operations/` directory). Match the user's name for the
project against a real `cwd` from that list.

If the project you want is **absent**, it has simply never been opened in
Session Manager. Do not invent a path and do not create the directory. Tell the
human: "open `<project>` in Session Manager once, then I can send this."

### 3. Write the proposal for the human who must approve it

The reader is a human in another repo who has never seen your code, cannot run
it, and must decide from the proposal alone whether to approve. A report that
says "the usual timeout thing again" is worthless across a repo boundary. Fill
each field:

- **`motivation`** (required, <=2000 chars) — *why* this matters, in the
  originating human's own terms (the goal they are pursuing), not the agent's
  internal reasoning. The receiver should be able to judge worth from this alone.
- **`plan`** (ordered steps, <=20; **required when `tag` is `feature`**) — what
  you propose the receiving project do, in order. Concrete enough to approve or
  reject step by step.
- **`acceptanceCriteria`** (required, 1-20) — checkable outcomes that tell the
  receiver the work is done. Each must be verifiable, not "works well".
- **`outOfScope`** (optional, <=20) — what this proposal deliberately does not
  ask for, so approval doesn't grow.
- **`body`** (required, <=20000 chars) — supporting evidence, not the pitch:
  - **Symptom** — what actually happened, with the real error text or output.
  - **Where you observed it** — your project, the call site, the version/commit
    if you know it.
  - **What you expected** — the contract you thought you were relying on.
  - **Suspected cause** — name a file in *their* repo if you have a candidate;
    say "I couldn't locate it from here" if you don't. Never fabricate a path.

Do not pass the sender Epic's own goal: the server records it automatically as
`originAsk`.

Attach real absolute paths worth reading via `referencePaths` rather than
pasting large files into the body (there is a 20 000-char body cap; the cap is
a signal, not an obstacle to route around).

#### Multi-part requests

Prefer **ONE proposal carrying the whole plan**: the receiver approves one
thing and sees every step. Split only when the parts are independently
approvable (each makes sense and ships without the others). When you split, send
every part with the same `series` `{key, title, total}` (`key` kebab-case
<=60, `title` <=120, `total` 2-50) and a correct `index` (1..total), and put a
one-paragraph summary of the overall plan inside each part's `motivation` so any
single part is understandable alone. A bare "step 5/7" with no overall plan is
exactly what this rule exists to prevent.

### 4. Deliver

```
feedback_open_session({
  toCwd:   "<absolute cwd from step 2>",
  fromCwd: "<your project's absolute cwd>",
  title:   "<one line — this becomes their queue row>",
  motivation: "<why this matters, in the human's terms>",
  plan: ["<step 1>", "<step 2>"],              // required when tag is feature
  acceptanceCriteria: ["<checkable outcome>"], // at least one
  outOfScope: ["<what this does not ask for>"],  // optional
  series: { key: "d2d-rollout", title: "D2D rollout", index: 2, total: 7 }, // optional, multi-part only
  body:    "<supporting evidence from step 3>",
  tag:     "bug" | "feature" | "discussion",   // default: discussion
  referencePaths: ["/abs/path", ...],          // optional
})
```

**Choosing the tag.** Default to `discussion`. `discussion` keeps `/develop`
available but never assumed — which is exactly right for a claim the receiving
project has not yet agreed with. Use `bug` or `feature` only when the finding is
unambiguous and you'd expect them to start decomposing it on sight (those two
treat PRD decomposition as the expected next step).

**Auto-start (only when the human asked).** If the human in THIS conversation
explicitly asked you to do the work in the other project, also pass
`autoStart: true` and `humanRequestQuote` — copied VERBATIM from their own
message, which must name the target project. Never write or paraphrase the
quote, and never pass `autoStart` for something you decided on your own: that
stays a plain proposal. If the quote cannot be verified, the call silently falls
back to a normal `proposed` session (the result note gives the reason), so
report it as a proposal in that case.

`fromEpicId` is filled in automatically from your running session; pass it
explicitly only if you know it and the auto-fill failed. When it resolves, a
receipt is chained onto your own session's event log so your transcript records
where the finding went.

### 5. Report honestly

Say exactly this much: the proposal was **delivered as a proposed session** in
`<toCwd>`, and it runs only if a human there presses **Approve & start**. That
human sees the motivation, plan and acceptance criteria on the proposal before
approving.

If the result status is `auto-approved`, say instead that the session was
auto-approved on the human's request and is starting in `<toCwd>` — not that it
is done.

Do **not** say the other project has been notified-and-is-working-on-it, that
the bug is filed/fixed/assigned, or that you'll follow up when they respond.
**There is no reply channel and no callback.** If the user needs an answer, the
next step is a human conversation, and you should say so.

## What this skill never does

- Write, edit or read-then-modify any file in the other project.
- Queue a PRD in the other project (a PRD may only join an already-approved
  Epic — the proposal you deliver is not approved).
- Start, resume or approve anything anywhere.
- Send to the project you're already in.
- Poll or wait for a response.

## If the tool isn't there

Two distinct failure modes — don't conflate them:

- **`feedback_open_session` errors with "app is not running"** — the Session
  Manager Electron app hosts the admin API that performs the cross-folder
  write. There is no fallback: hand-writing another project's
  `active-index.json` is exactly the racing second writer the single-writer law
  exists to prevent. Tell the human to start the app, and report the finding to
  them in the meantime so it isn't lost.
- **`feedback_open_session` is absent from your tool list entirely** — the
  `session-manager-scheduler` MCP server isn't registered for this project.
  That's a misconfiguration, not an offline app. Fix:
  `claude mcp add session-manager-scheduler --scope user -- node <session-manager-repo>/scripts/scheduler-mcp-server.cjs`
  (once at user scope covers every project).

# Scene & Data Structure

Blender uses a datablock system - objects and their underlying data (meshes, materials,
cameras, etc.) are separate entities.

Hierarchy:
  * **Scene** - top-level container. A .blend can have multiple.
  * **View Layer** - controls collection visibility/selectability.
  * **Collection** - organizational tree. Objects live in collections; can be nested;
    objects can belong to multiple collections.
  * **Object** - has a transform (location, rotation, scale) and references underlying data
    (Mesh, Curve, Camera, etc.). Multiple objects can share the same data (linked duplicates).
  * **Datablocks** - the actual data: geometry, materials, textures, etc.

Key concepts:
  * Objects and data are separate - deleting one does not delete the other.
  * Orphaned datablocks (zero users) are purged on save/reload or manual purge.
  * Objects created via the data API must be linked to a collection to appear in a scene.
  * Shared data: check user count before modifying a datablock - editing a shared mesh
    affects all objects referencing it. Make single-user first if needed.
  * In most cases file assets:
    * Images, Fonts, Sounds, other `.blend` files -  corraspond to a data-block.

Visibility has three independent states:
  * **Viewport hidden** - still fully scriptable.
  * **Disabled in view layer** - excluded; may be inaccessible to view-layer-dependent operators.
  * **Disabled for render** - skipped during render, otherwise normal.
Check these when objects seem "missing" or operators skip them.

Blender defaults to meters. Check scene unit settings before creating dimensioned objects.

Exploring scenes:
  * Walk the collection hierarchy for an overview first.
  * Don't dump entire scenes - inspect progressively for large scenes.
  * Check object types, parenting, modifiers, and materials before making changes.

# send-feedback

**Role:** the ONE channel for project-to-project communication. You are a
*courier*, never a fixer — you deliver a report into another project's inbox
and stop. You never edit the other project's files, never queue a PRD there,
and never wait for a reply.

## Why this exists

`/process-feedback`, `/my-feedback` and the `session-manager-operations/feedback/`
folder were retired (2026-08-02), and the scheduler was locked down so a PRD can
only JOIN an Epic a human already approved. Both were right. Together they left
no way to hand a finding across a project boundary. This skill is that way back
— narrowed to exactly one shape: **a proposal deposited in another project's
queue, which a human there must approve before anything runs.**

## The one hard rule

**Different project, or don't use this.** If the finding belongs to the project
you are already working in, run `/develop` inside the Epic you are already in.
The tool refuses `toCwd === fromCwd` outright, so getting this wrong costs you a
round-trip, not a wrong write.

| Finding belongs to | Route |
| --- | --- |
| The project you're in | `/develop` in your current Epic |
| Another project on this machine | this skill |
| Nothing actionable | say so explicitly |

Per the global core rules, routing a finding is the **default action, not a
question**. Do not ask "should I send this to X?" — send it, then report what
you delivered.

## Steps

### 1. Confirm it's really theirs

Before couriering anything, satisfy yourself the finding is about the other
project's behavior, not about how *your* project calls it. A misrouted report
costs a human in another repo their attention. If you can't tell, say which
project you think owns it and why, and send it anyway with that uncertainty
stated in the body — an honest "I think this is yours because X, but I couldn't
verify from here" is useful; a confident wrong claim is not.

### 2. Resolve the target cwd — never guess it

```
feedback_list_projects()
```

Returns every project on this machine that can receive feedback (each already
has a `session-manager-operations/` directory). Match the user's name for the
project against a real `cwd` from that list.

If the project you want is **absent**, it has simply never been opened in
Session Manager. Do not invent a path and do not create the directory. Tell the
human: "open `<project>` in Session Manager once, then I can send this."

### 3. Write the proposal for the human who must approve it

The reader is a human in another repo who has never seen your code, cannot run
it, and must decide from the proposal alone whether to approve. A report that
says "the usual timeout thing again" is worthless across a repo boundary. Fill
each field:

- **`motivation`** (required, <=2000 chars) — *why* this matters, in the
  originating human's own terms (the goal they are pursuing), not the agent's
  internal reasoning. The receiver should be able to judge worth from this alone.
- **`plan`** (ordered steps, <=20; **required when `tag` is `feature`**) — what
  you propose the receiving project do, in order. Concrete enough to approve or
  reject step by step.
- **`acceptanceCriteria`** (required, 1-20) — checkable outcomes that tell the
  receiver the work is done. Each must be verifiable, not "works well".
- **`outOfScope`** (optional, <=20) — what this proposal deliberately does not
  ask for, so approval doesn't grow.
- **`body`** (required, <=20000 chars) — supporting evidence, not the pitch:
  - **Symptom** — what actually happened, with the real error text or output.
  - **Where you observed it** — your project, the call site, the version/commit
    if you know it.
  - **What you expected** — the contract you thought you were relying on.
  - **Suspected cause** — name a file in *their* repo if you have a candidate;
    say "I couldn't locate it from here" if you don't. Never fabricate a path.

Do not pass the sender Epic's own goal: the server records it automatically as
`originAsk`.

Attach real absolute paths worth reading via `referencePaths` rather than
pasting large files into the body (there is a 20 000-char body cap; the cap is
a signal, not an obstacle to route around).

#### Multi-part requests

Prefer **ONE proposal carrying the whole plan**: the receiver approves one
thing and sees every step. Split only when the parts are independently
approvable (each makes sense and ships without the others). When you split, send
every part with the same `series` `{key, title, total}` (`key` kebab-case
<=60, `title` <=120, `total` 2-50) and a correct `index` (1..total), and put a
one-paragraph summary of the overall plan inside each part's `motivation` so any
single part is understandable alone. A bare "step 5/7" with no overall plan is
exactly what this rule exists to prevent.

### 4. Deliver

```
feedback_open_session({
  toCwd:   "<absolute cwd from step 2>",
  fromCwd: "<your project's absolute cwd>",
  title:   "<one line — this becomes their queue row>",
  motivation: "<why this matters, in the human's terms>",
  plan: ["<step 1>", "<step 2>"],              // required when tag is feature
  acceptanceCriteria: ["<checkable outcome>"], // at least one
  outOfScope: ["<what this does not ask for>"],  // optional
  series: { key: "d2d-rollout", title: "D2D rollout", index: 2, total: 7 }, // optional, multi-part only
  body:    "<supporting evidence from step 3>",
  tag:     "bug" | "feature" | "discussion",   // default: discussion
  referencePaths: ["/abs/path", ...],          // optional
})
```

**Choosing the tag.** Default to `discussion`. `discussion` keeps `/develop`
available but never assumed — which is exactly right for a claim the receiving
project has not yet agreed with. Use `bug` or `feature` only when the finding is
unambiguous and you'd expect them to start decomposing it on sight (those two
treat PRD decomposition as the expected next step).

**Auto-start (only when the human asked).** If the human in THIS conversation
explicitly asked you to do the work in the other project, also pass
`autoStart: true` and `humanRequestQuote` — copied VERBATIM from their own
message, which must name the target project. Never write or paraphrase the
quote, and never pass `autoStart` for something you decided on your own: that
stays a plain proposal. If the quote cannot be verified, the call silently falls
back to a normal `proposed` session (the result note gives the reason), so
report it as a proposal in that case.

`fromEpicId` is filled in automatically from your running session; pass it
explicitly only if you know it and the auto-fill failed. When it resolves, a
receipt is chained onto your own session's event log so your transcript records
where the finding went.

### 5. Report honestly

Say exactly this much: the proposal was **delivered as a proposed session** in
`<toCwd>`, and it runs only if a human there presses **Approve & start**. That
human sees the motivation, plan and acceptance criteria on the proposal before
approving.

If the result status is `auto-approved`, say instead that the session was
auto-approved on the human's request and is starting in `<toCwd>` — not that it
is done.

Do **not** say the other project has been notified-and-is-working-on-it, that
the bug is filed/fixed/assigned, or that you'll follow up when they respond.
**There is no reply channel and no callback.** If the user needs an answer, the
next step is a human conversation, and you should say so.

## What this skill never does

- Write, edit or read-then-modify any file in the other project.
- Queue a PRD in the other project (a PRD may only join an already-approved
  Epic — the proposal you deliver is not approved).
- Start, resume or approve anything anywhere.
- Send to the project you're already in.
- Poll or wait for a response.

## If the tool isn't there

Two distinct failure modes — don't conflate them:

- **`feedback_open_session` errors with "app is not running"** — the Session
  Manager Electron app hosts the admin API that performs the cross-folder
  write. There is no fallback: hand-writing another project's
  `active-index.json` is exactly the racing second writer the single-writer law
  exists to prevent. Tell the human to start the app, and report the finding to
  them in the meantime so it isn't lost.
- **`feedback_open_session` is absent from your tool list entirely** — the
  `session-manager-scheduler` MCP server isn't registered for this project.
  That's a misconfiguration, not an offline app. Fix:
  `claude mcp add session-manager-scheduler --scope user -- node <session-manager-repo>/scripts/scheduler-mcp-server.cjs`
  (once at user scope covers every project).

# MCP Server Instructions

The following MCP servers have provided instructions for how to use their tools and resources:

## blender
You have access to Blender tools to interact with a Blender scene directly.
Blender must be running with the MCP add-on enabled and connected.

IMPORTANT: Respect existing structure and naming conventions.
NEVER assume missing values - inspect the scene first.
Do not destructively modify objects without confirmation.

# Bundled Manuals

Reference documentation is bundled alongside this server as plain-text RST files.
Search and read them directly with standard text tools (grep, file read, etc.):
  * `data/api/` - Blender Python API reference (RST files per module/class).
    Consult when writing or debugging `bpy` code: operator signatures, type
    properties, enum values, etc.
  * `data/manual/` - Blender user manual (RST files mirroring the official manual structure).
    Consult for conceptual explanations, workflow guidance, and feature overviews.

# Executing Code

The `execute_blender_code` tool runs Python code via `bpy` in the connected Blender instance.

The `execute_blender_code` tool is a last resort, if there are other tools that provide
the functionality you need, use those instead.

Prefer operators (`bpy.ops`) for standard actions (adding primitives, applying modifiers,
setting origins) - they handle defaults and context. Use the data API (`bpy.data`) for
precise control or to avoid side effects.

Many operators depend on the current mode (Object, Edit, Sculpt, etc.) and which objects
are active/selected. Verify or set the mode first - wrong mode either fails or silently
does nothing.

The **active object** and **selection** are distinct. Many operators require both.
Set them explicitly - do not assume the current state. Operators change selection and
active state as a side effect, so re-set both between sequential operator calls on
different objects.

Update the dependency graph after changes before reading computed properties
(world matrices, modifier results, etc.).

In edit mode, access mesh geometry through the bmesh API, not the regular mesh data API.
Flush bmesh changes back to the mesh - forgetting this silently loses all edits.

Return structured data (dicts, lists) from executed code, not print output.

# Scene & Data Structure

Blender uses a datablock system - objects and their underlying data (meshes, materials,
cameras, etc.) are separate entities.

Hierarchy:
  * **Scene** - top-level container. A .blend can have multiple.
  * **View Layer** - controls collection visibility/selectability.
  * **Collection** - organizational tree. Objects live in collections; can be nested;
    objects can belong to multiple collections.
  * **Object** - has a transform (location, rotation, scale) and references underlying data
    (Mesh, Curve, Camera, etc.). Multiple objects can share the same data (linked duplicates).
  * **Datablocks** - the actual data: geometry, materials, textures, etc.

Key concepts:
  * Objects and data are separate - deleting one does not delete the other.
  * Orphaned datablocks (zero users) are purged on save/reload or manual purge.
  * Objects created via the data API must be linked to a collection to appear in a scene.
  * Shared data: check user count before modifying a datablock - editing a shared mesh
    affects all objects referencing it. Make single-user first if needed.
  * In most cases file assets:
    * Images, Fonts, Sounds, other `.blend` files -  corraspond to a data-block.

Visibility has three independent states:
  * **Viewport hidden** - still fully scriptable.
  * **Disabled in view layer** - excluded; may be inaccessible to view-layer-dependent operators.
  * **Disabled for render** - skipped during render, otherwise normal.
Check these when objects seem "missing" or operators skip them.

Blender defaults to meters. Check scene unit settings before creating dimensioned objects.

Exploring scenes:
  * Walk the collection hierarchy for an overview first.
  * Don't dump entire scenes - inspect progressively for large scenes.
  * Check object types, parenting, modifiers, and materials before making changes.

bilko.run now has ONE site-wide session identity: first-party cookies bilko_vid (visitor UUID, 1 year) and bilko_sid (session UUID, 30-minute sliding idle, shared across tabs). Everything joins on them: server page hits, the server-injected click beacon, host-kit telemetry, and /api/telemetry/* ingest (the server stamps records with the cookie ids). An admin Sessions view (landing -> pages -> clicks -> events -> errors) and a Flows view (per-app health + per-flow step funnels) are being built at /admin/observability.

WHAT IS AUTOMATIC (no code): every HTML page served under /projects/<slug>/ gets the beacon injected by the host. WHAT THIS APP MUST ADD (the taxonomy; use these names exactly so the dashboard groups them):

Everything joins on them: server page hits, the server-injected click beacon, host-kit telemetry, and /api/telemetry/* ingest (the server stamps records with the cookie ids). An admin Sessions view (landing -> pages -> clicks -> events -> errors) and a Flows view (per-app health + per-flow step funnels) are being built at /admin/observability.

WHAT IS AUTOMATIC (no code): every HTML page served under /projects/<slug>/ gets the beacon injected by the host. It records page views on load and on SPA history navigation, and clicks on a, button, [role=button], summary and [data-track]. Click labels are scrubbed of emails and long digit runs, and hrefs lose their query strings.

WHAT THIS APP MUST ADD (the taxonomy; use these names exactly so the dashboard groups them):
1. Pages: every route is already auto-captured. Screens that do NOT change the URL (game states, wizards, modals that act as pages) must emit track('screen_view', { screen: '<kebab-name>' }) on each change.
2. Main buttons: every primary button/link gets data-track="<area>-<action>" (kebab-case, unique within the app, e.g. hero-start, nav-docs, results-share). Wrap anything that could show personal text in data-track-redact.
3. Primary flows: pick the 3-5 flows that matter and call trackFlow(flow, step, props?) from host-kit. flow and step must match /^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,39}$/. Emit a start step and a success step at least (plus a fail step where one exists).
4. Monetization (explicitly required wherever it exists: buy, subscribe, tip, credits, paid tier, claim):
   - buttons use data-track prefixes buy- / subscribe- / tip-
   - trackFlow('checkout', step), steps: view-offer, click-buy, checkout-redirect, success, cancel; props { product, plan? }
   - tips: trackFlow('tip', step), steps: click-tip, checkout-redirect, success
5. Downloads (explicitly required wherever they exist: zips, installers, exports, files):
   - buttons use the data-track prefix download-
   - trackFlow('download', step), steps: click-download, download-started, download-failed; props { artifact, version, platform }
6. PII: never put emails, names, tokens, free-text input or payment amounts tied to a person in props. host-kit's stripPII redacts keys matching email|password|token|key|ssn|card|cvv|apikey.

bilko.run now has ONE site-wide session identity: first-party cookies bilko_vid (visitor UUID, 1 year) and bilko_sid (session UUID, 30-minute sliding idle, shared across tabs). Everything joins on them: server page hits, the server-injected click beacon, host-kit telemetry, and /api/telemetry/* ingest (the server stamps records with the cookie ids). An admin Sessions view (landing -> pages -> clicks -> events -> errors) and a Flows view (per-app health + per-flow step funnels) are being built at /admin/observability.

WHAT IS AUTOMATIC (no code): every HTML page served under /projects/<slug>/ gets the beacon injected by the host. It records page views on load and on SPA history navigation, and clicks on a, button, [role=button], summary and [data-track]. Click labels are scrubbed of emails and long digit runs, and hrefs lose their query strings.

WHAT THIS APP MUST ADD (the taxonomy; use these names exactly so the dashboard groups them):
1. Pages: every route is already auto-captured. Screens that do NOT change the URL (game states, wizards, modals that act as pages) must emit track('screen_view', { screen: '<kebab-name>' }) on each change.
2. Main buttons: every primary button/link gets data-track="<area>-<action>" (kebab-case, unique within the app, e.g. hero-start, nav-docs, results-share). Wrap anything that could show personal text in data-track-redact.
3. Primary flows: pick the 3-5 flows that matter and call trackFlow(flow, step, props?) from host-kit. flow and step must match /^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,39}$/. Emit a start step and a success step at least (plus a fail step where one exists).
4. Monetization (explicitly required wherever it exists: buy, subscribe, tip, credits, paid tier, claim):
   - buttons use data-track prefixes buy- / subscribe- / tip-
   - trackFlow('checkout', step), steps: view-offer, click-buy, checkout-redirect, success, cancel; props { product, plan? }
   - tips: trackFlow('tip', step), steps: click-tip, checkout-redirect, success
5. Downloads (explicitly required wherever they exist: zips, installers, exports, files):
   - buttons use the data-track prefix download-
   - trackFlow('download', step), steps: click-download, download-started, download-failed; props { artifact, version, platform }
6. PII: never put emails, names, tokens, free-text input or payment amounts tied to a person in props. host-kit's stripPII redacts keys matching email|password|token|key|ssn|card|cvv|apikey.

HOW TO SEND:
- Apps that bundle JS: depend on host-kit ("host-kit": "file:../Bilko/packages/host-kit"; dist/ was rebuilt on 2026-10-18 with trackFlow), then run pnpm install. Call initTelemetry({ app: '<registry slug>', version }) once at boot, then import { track, trackFlow } from 'host-kit'. host-kit now posts same-origin to /api/telemetry on bilko.run.
- Plain HTML or no bundler: data-track attributes cover buttons. For flows, use navigator.sendBeacon('/api/telemetry/event', JSON.stringify({ batch: [{ app: '<slug>', name: flow + '.' + step, ts: Date.now(), props: { flow: flow, step: step, path: location.pathname } }] })). The server fills in the session ids from the cookie.
- Canonical doc (landing in the host repo): ~/Projects/Bilko/docs/observability.md, section "Tagging taxonomy". Host-kit source: ~/Projects/Bilko/packages/host-kit/src/telemetry.ts.

STATUS AND CAVEATS:
- The host-kit SDK change (commit 6b739f30) and the telemetry cookie stamping (5a111ab9) are committed on Bilko's local main, but not yet pushed or deployed.
- Beacon data-track capture and the admin dashboards are still being built.
- So: tag now, verify payloads in browser devtools (Network: /api/telemetry/event and /api/analytics/click), and republish to bilko.run through your normal publish step. Dashboard verification follows once the host side deploys.

Everything joins on them: server page hits, the server-injected click beacon, host-kit telemetry, and /api/telemetry/* ingest (the server stamps records with the cookie ids). An admin Sessions view (landing -> pages -> clicks -> events -> errors) and a Flows view (per-app health + per-flow step funnels) are being built at /admin/observability.

WHAT IS AUTOMATIC (no code): every HTML page served under /projects/<slug>/ gets the beacon injected by the host. It records page views on load and on SPA history navigation, and clicks on a, button, [role=button], summary and [data-track]. Click labels are scrubbed of emails and long digit runs, and hrefs lose their query strings.

WHAT THIS APP MUST ADD (the taxonomy; use these names exactly so the dashboard groups them):
1. Pages: every route is already auto-captured. Screens that do NOT change the URL (game states, wizards, modals that act as pages) must emit track('screen_view', { screen: '<kebab-name>' }) on each change.
2. Main buttons: every primary button/link gets data-track="<area>-<action>" (kebab-case, unique within the app, e.g. hero-start, nav-docs, results-share). Wrap anything that could show personal text in data-track-redact.
3. Primary flows: pick the 3-5 flows that matter and call trackFlow(flow, step, props?) from host-kit. flow and step must match /^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,39}$/. Emit a start step and a success step at least (plus a fail step where one exists).
4. Monetization (explicitly required wherever it exists: buy, subscribe, tip, credits, paid tier, claim):
   - buttons use data-track prefixes buy- / subscribe- / tip-
   - trackFlow('checkout', step), steps: view-offer, click-buy, checkout-redirect, success, cancel; props { product, plan? }
   - tips: trackFlow('tip', step), steps: click-tip, checkout-redirect, success
5. Downloads (explicitly required wherever they exist: zips, installers, exports, files):
   - buttons use the data-track prefix download-
   - trackFlow('download', step), steps: click-download, download-started, download-failed; props { artifact, version, platform }
6. PII: never put emails, names, tokens, free-text input or payment amounts tied to a person in props. host-kit's stripPII redacts keys matching email|password|token|key|ssn|card|cvv|apikey.

- Apps that bundle JS: depend on host-kit ("host-kit": "file:../Bilko/packages/host-kit"; dist/ was rebuilt on 2026-10-18 with trackFlow), then run pnpm install. - Plain HTML or no bundler: data-track attributes cover buttons. For flows, use navigator.sendBeacon('/api/telemetry/event', JSON.stringify({ batch: [{ app: '<slug>', name: flow + '.' + step, ts: Date.now(), props: { flow: flow, step: step, path: location.pathname } }] })). The `execute_blender_code` tool runs Python code via `bpy` in the connected Blender instance.

The `execute_blender_code` tool is a last resort, if there are other tools that provide

# Scene & Data Structure

Blender uses a datablock system - objects and their underlying data (meshes, materials,
cameras, etc.) are separate entities.

Hierarchy:
  * **Scene** - top-level container. A .blend can have multiple.
  * **View Layer** - controls collection visibility/selectability.
  * **Collection** - organizational tree. Objects live in collections; can be nested;
    objects can belong to multiple collections.
  * **Object** - has a transform (location, rotation, scale) and references underlying data
    (Mesh, Curve, Camera, etc.). Multiple objects can share the same data (linked duplicates).
  * **Datablocks** - the actual data: geometry, materials, textures, etc.

Key concepts:
  * Objects and data are separate - deleting one does not delete the other.
  * Orphaned datablocks (zero users) are purged on save/reload or manual purge.
  * Objects created via the data API must be linked to a collection to appear in a scene.
  * Shared data: check user count before modifying a datablock - editing a shared mesh
    affects all objects referencing it. Make single-user first if needed.
  * In most cases file assets:
    * Images, Fonts, Sounds, other `.blend` files -  corraspond to a data-block.

Visibility has three independent states:
  * **Viewport hidden** - still fully scriptable.
  * **Disabled in view layer** - excluded; may be inaccessible to view-layer-dependent operators.
  * **Disabled for render** - skipped during render, otherwise normal.
Check these when objects seem "missing" or operators skip them.

Blender defaults to meters. Check scene unit settings before creating dimensioned objects.

Exploring scenes:
  * Walk the collection hierarchy for an overview first.
  * Don't dump entire scenes - inspect progressively for large scenes.
  * Check object types, parenting, modifiers, and materials before making changes.

The `execute_blender_code` tool runs Python code via `bpy` in the connected Blender instance.

# Scene & Data Structure

Blender uses a datablock system - objects and their underlying data (meshes, materials,
cameras, etc.) are separate entities.

Hierarchy:
  * **Scene** - top-level container. A .blend can have multiple.
  * **View Layer** - controls collection visibility/selectability.
  * **Collection** - organizational tree. Objects live in collections; can be nested;
    objects can belong to multiple collections.
  * **Object** - has a transform (location, rotation, scale) and references underlying data
    (Mesh, Curve, Camera, etc.). Multiple objects can share the same data (linked duplicates).
  * **Datablocks** - the actual data: geometry, materials, textures, etc.

Key concepts:
  * Objects and data are separate - deleting one does not delete the other.
  * Orphaned datablocks (zero users) are purged on save/reload or manual purge.
  * Objects created via the data API must be linked to a collection to appear in a scene.
  * Shared data: check user count before modifying a datablock - editing a shared mesh
    affects all objects referencing it. Make single-user first if needed.
  * In most cases file assets:
    * Images, Fonts, Sounds, other `.blend` files -  corraspond to a data-block.

Visibility has three independent states:
  * **Viewport hidden** - still fully scriptable.
  * **Disabled in view layer** - excluded; may be inaccessible to view-layer-dependent operators.
  * **Disabled for render** - skipped during render, otherwise normal.
Check these when objects seem "missing" or operators skip them.

Blender defaults to meters. Check scene unit settings before creating dimensioned objects.

Exploring scenes:
  * Walk the collection hierarchy for an overview first.
  * Don't dump entire scenes - inspect progressively for large scenes.
  * Check object types, parenting, modifiers, and materials before making changes.

# MCP Server Instructions

The following MCP servers have provided instructions for how to use their tools and resources:

## blender
You have access to Blender tools to interact with a Blender scene directly.
Blender must be running with the MCP add-on enabled and connected.

IMPORTANT: Respect existing structure and naming conventions.
NEVER assume missing values - inspect the scene first.
Do not destructively modify objects without confirmation.

# Bundled Manuals

Reference documentation is bundled alongside this server as plain-text RST files.
Search and read them directly with standard text tools (grep, file read, etc.):
  * `data/api/` - Blender Python API reference (RST files per module/class).
    Consult when writing or debugging `bpy` code: operator signatures, type
    properties, enum values, etc.
  * `data/manual/` - Blender user manual (RST files mirroring the official manual structure).
    Consult for conceptual explanations, workflow guidance, and feature overviews.

# Executing Code

The `execute_blender_code` tool runs Python code via `bpy` in the connected Blender instance.

The `execute_blender_code` tool is a last resort, if there are other tools that provide
the functionality you need, use those instead.

Prefer operators (`bpy.ops`) for standard actions (adding primitives, applying modifiers,
setting origins) - they handle defaults and context. Use the data API (`bpy.data`) for
precise control or to avoid side effects.

Many operators depend on the current mode (Object, Edit, Sculpt, etc.) and which objects
are active/selected. Verify or set the mode first - wrong mode either fails or silently
does nothing.

The **active object** and **selection** are distinct. Many operators require both.
Set them explicitly - do not assume the current state. Operators change selection and
active state as a side effect, so re-set both between sequential operator calls on
different objects.

Update the dependency graph after changes before reading computed properties
(world matrices, modifier results, etc.).

In edit mode, access mesh geometry through the bmesh API, not the regular mesh data API.
Flush bmesh changes back to the mesh - forgetting this silently loses all edits.

Return structured data (dicts, lists) from executed code, not print output.

# Scene & Data Structure

Blender uses a datablock system - objects and their underlying data (meshes, materials,
cameras, etc.) are separate entities.

Hierarchy:
  * **Scene** - top-level container. A .blend can have multiple.
  * **View Layer** - controls collection visibility/selectability.
  * **Collection** - organizational tree. Objects live in collections; can be nested;
    objects can belong to multiple collections.
  * **Object** - has a transform (location, rotation, scale) and references underlying data
    (Mesh, Curve, Camera, etc.). Multiple objects can share the same data (linked duplicates).
  * **Datablocks** - the actual data: geometry, materials, textures, etc.

Key concepts:
  * Objects and data are separate - deleting one does not delete the other.
  * Orphaned datablocks (zero users) are purged on save/reload or manual purge.
  * Objects created via the data API must be linked to a collection to appear in a scene.
  * Shared data: check user count before modifying a datablock - editing a shared mesh
    affects all objects referencing it. Make single-user first if needed.
  * In most cases file assets:
    * Images, Fonts, Sounds, other `.blend` files -  corraspond to a data-block.

Visibility has three independent states:
  * **Viewport hidden** - still fully scriptable.
  * **Disabled in view layer** - excluded; may be inaccessible to view-layer-dependent operators.
  * **Disabled for render** - skipped during render, otherwise normal.
Check these when objects seem "missing" or operators skip them.

Blender defaults to meters. Check scene unit settings before creating dimensioned objects.

Exploring scenes:
  * Walk the collection hierarchy for an overview first.
  * Don't dump entire scenes - inspect progressively for large scenes.
  * Check object types, parenting, modifiers, and materials before making changes.

# Bundled Manuals

# Executing Code

The `execute_blender_code` tool runs Python code via `bpy` in the connected Blender instance.

The `execute_blender_code` tool is a last resort, if there are other tools that provide
the functionality you need, use those instead.

Prefer operators (`bpy.ops`) for standard actions (adding primitives, applying modifiers,
setting origins) - they handle defaults and context. Use the data API (`bpy.data`) for
precise control or to avoid side effects.

Many operators depend on the current mode (Object, Edit, Sculpt, etc.) and which objects
are active/selected. Verify or set the mode first - wrong mode either fails or silently
does nothing.

The **active object** and **selection** are distinct. Many operators require both.
Set them explicitly - do not assume the current state. Operators change selection and
active state as a side effect, so re-set both between sequential operator calls on
different objects.

Update the dependency graph after changes before reading computed properties
(world matrices, modifier results, etc.).

In edit mode, access mesh geometry through the bmesh API, not the regular mesh data API.
Flush bmesh changes back to the mesh - forgetting this silently loses all edits.

Return structured data (dicts, lists) from executed code, not print output.

# Scene & Data Structure

Blender uses a datablock system - objects and their underlying data (meshes, materials,
cameras, etc.) are separate entities.

Hierarchy:
  * **Scene** - top-level container. A .blend can have multiple.
  * **View Layer** - controls collection visibility/selectability.
  * **Collection** - organizational tree. Objects live in collections; can be nested;
    objects can belong to multiple collections.
  * **Object** - has a transform (location, rotation, scale) and references underlying data
    (Mesh, Curve, Camera, etc.). Multiple objects can share the same data (linked duplicates).
  * **Datablocks** - the actual data: geometry, materials, textures, etc.

Key concepts:
  * Objects and data are separate - deleting one does not delete the other.
  * Orphaned datablocks (zero users) are purged on save/reload or manual purge.
  * Objects created via the data API must be linked to a collection to appear in a scene.
  * Shared data: check user count before modifying a datablock - editing a shared mesh
    affects all objects referencing it. Make single-user first if needed.
  * In most cases file assets:
    * Images, Fonts, Sounds, other `.blend` files -  corraspond to a data-block.

Visibility has three independent states:
  * **Viewport hidden** - still fully scriptable.
  * **Disabled in view layer** - excluded; may be inaccessible to view-layer-dependent operators.
  * **Disabled for render** - skipped during render, otherwise normal.
Check these when objects seem "missing" or operators skip them.

Blender defaults to meters. Check scene unit settings before creating dimensioned objects.

Exploring scenes:
  * Walk the collection hierarchy for an overview first.
  * Don't dump entire scenes - inspect progressively for large scenes.
  * Check object types, parenting, modifiers, and materials before making changes.

# Scene & Data Structure

Blender uses a datablock system - objects and their underlying data (meshes, materials,
cameras, etc.) are separate entities.

Hierarchy:
  * **Scene** - top-level container. A .blend can have multiple.
  * **View Layer** - controls collection visibility/selectability.
  * **Collection** - organizational tree. Objects live in collections; can be nested;
    objects can belong to multiple collections.
  * **Object** - has a transform (location, rotation, scale) and references underlying data
    (Mesh, Curve, Camera, etc.). Multiple objects can share the same data (linked duplicates).
  * **Datablocks** - the actual data: geometry, materials, textures, etc.

Key concepts:
  * Objects and data are separate - deleting one does not delete the other.
  * Orphaned datablocks (zero users) are purged on save/reload or manual purge.
  * Objects created via the data API must be linked to a collection to appear in a scene.
  * Shared data: check user count before modifying a datablock - editing a shared mesh
    affects all objects referencing it. Make single-user first if needed.
  * In most cases file assets:
    * Images, Fonts, Sounds, other `.blend` files -  corraspond to a data-block.

Visibility has three independent states:
  * **Viewport hidden** - still fully scriptable.
  * **Disabled in view layer** - excluded; may be inaccessible to view-layer-dependent operators.
  * **Disabled for render** - skipped during render, otherwise normal.
Check these when objects seem "missing" or operators skip them.

Blender defaults to meters. Check scene unit settings before creating dimensioned objects.

Exploring scenes:
  * Walk the collection hierarchy for an overview first.
  * Don't dump entire scenes - inspect progressively for large scenes.
  * Check object types, parenting, modifiers, and materials before making changes.

**src/pages/admin/SessionsPanel.tsx**
15. minimalism, :24-66, :79-82, :112-138, :235-276 — the inline journey is now a second, weaker copy of Session View, and every row already links there. Fix: make the panel list-only.

17. bug, :193-199 — the Apps field only counts apps that sent events or errors. Sessions that only viewed apps show "—", while the list shows those apps (from the server). Fix: return `apps` from `/api/admin/sessions/:id`.

**The review** checked the observability code for clarity and minimalism. It found 3 real bugs, confirmed the 4 known minor issues plus 2 smaller ones the validators had flagged, and found that most of the extra code was duplication in the admin dashboard pages. Its verdict was that the server design is sound.

**The 3 bugs:**
- **Project card clicks all record the same name.** On `/projects`, the click beacon never reads the `data-track-slug` attribute, so you can't tell which project was clicked.
- **The download funnel is inflated.** The Field Manual records a download for a link that only opens the product page, and it labels manual-file downloads as the Session Manager app.
- **The Session View header shows apps wrong.** Its Apps field only counts apps that sent events or errors, so a session that just viewed an app shows "—".

**Queued, in order of when they can run:**

| # | PRD | What it fixes | Runs after |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1375 | cleanup-server-session-identity | Removes three untyped `bilkoIds` lookups, makes the `/api` exclusion exact, simplifies the page-hits fallback, fixes stale comments, and documents that `visitor_id` means two different things in different tables | — |
| 1376 | cleanup-admin-sessions-api | One shared timeline type instead of three, one validator for the `app` filter (both routes return 400 on a bad value), no string-patched SQL, and the session detail now returns its apps | — |
| 1377 | cleanup-host-kit-telemetry | Logs and errors no longer write the session cookies twice per call, and ids stop falling back to `'anon'` where `crypto.randomUUID` is missing | — |
| 1378 | cleanup-host-telemetry-module | One send helper instead of two, consistent constants, and the unused `trackScreen` removed | — |
| 1379 | cleanup-session-player-format | A shared `?step=` link means the same step in "All" and "Clicks only" mode; events no longer start fake pages; time formatters move into `src/lib/format.ts` | 1376 |
| 1380 | cleanup-session-view-list | The Sessions panel becomes list-only and also serves as the Session View's picker, which removes a duplicate timeline and list; adds dark mode, fixes the `colSpan` typo, shows apps from the API | 1379 |
| 1381 | cleanup-click-tagging | Fixes the project-click and download-funnel bugs; the Session Manager header's tip event gets the `area` field the others have | 1378 |
| 1382 | validate-observability-cleanup | Also checks there are no leftover duplicates, that the admin pages got smaller, and that the full test suite passes | all |

**What I didn't adopt:**
- **Having the host site use host-kit for its own telemetry.** It would add host-kit's global error handlers to the host site, and local dev would send events to production. The host module gets slimmed down in #1378 instead.
- **Dropping the unused `funnel_events(visitor_id)` index.** It already exists in production, and removing it would cost more than leaving it.
- **A shared 1/7/30-day toggle component.** It would mean editing older admin panels that aren't part of this work.

**TL;DR — Bilko is a host platform, not a product.** Every "tool" is an independent app that uses Bilko's auth, credits, component kit, and brand chrome. Long-term goal: every app lives in its own sibling repo under `~/Projects/`, built in its own Claude session, and hosted on bilko.run via the **static-path contract**.

**Git repo:** this is **`StanislavBG/bilko-run`**, remote `origin`, branch `main`. That is the one and only repo for the Bilko platform — commit and push here. The `content-grade` remote (`Content-Grade/Content-Grade`) is a **separate, unrelated project**; its history has diverged and you must **never push Bilko to it**. (Older docs/scripts that say "push to both remotes" or "deploy from Content-Grade master" are obsolete — see [Deploy](#tech-stack) and [Rules](#rules).)

**Repo map:** see README.md → "Where things live" for the folder-by-folder layout.

**Authoritative spec:** [`docs/host-contract.md`](docs/host-contract.md) — read it before adding, removing, or migrating any app.

**For Claude sessions working on a sibling app repo (not this one):** Use the [`bilko-host` MCP](mcp-host-server/README.md) to register, publish, and inspect apps. You don't need to edit this repo by hand.

## What This Is

bilko.run is Bilko's personal brand site and host platform. Apps share a common credit model ($1/credit or $5/7 credits via Stripe), shared Clerk auth, shared Stripe wallet, and a shared component kit. Each app is its own product with its own page, scoring engine, and UX — they are NOT features of one product.

### Current apps

**In-repo (react-route, canonical URL `/products/<slug>`):** **Session Manager** is the one react-route app (`/products/session-manager`, plus its Field Manual at `/products/session-manager/manual`). All 9 AI tools have been extracted to sibling repos. Beyond that the host repo ships only brand chrome (Layout, HomePage, ProjectsPage, BlogPage, PricingPage, AdminPage).

**Sibling repos (static-path, canonical URL `/projects/<slug>/`)** — fully independent, built in their own Claude sessions. **Architectural note — gateway pattern for the 8 AI-tool siblings:** StackAudit, LaunchGrader, AdScorer, HeadlineGrader, ThreadGrader, EmailForge, AudienceDecoder, and PageRoast each ship their React page from the sibling repo, but their Gemini-backed scoring endpoint stays in Bilko host under `server/routes/tools/<slug>.ts`.
